item.title: RFK Jr. Leaves Anti-Arab Remarks Unanswered At Detroit Health Visit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. declined to address his false claims about Arab science as CAIR called for his removal from office.
item.content:encoded:
Robert F. Kennedy Jr. left his anti-Arab remarks unanswered at a Detroit health visit as a civil rights group demanded that he lose his Cabinet job.

The Council on American-Islamic Relations called for the health secretary’s immediate firing. The Muslim civil rights group tied its demand to his job running a federal agency whose work reaches Americans across ethnic and religious lines.

In its statement, CAIR called the remarks “utterly disqualifying for public office.” It also noted that his attack swept in Muslim and Christian Arab Americans.

Kennedy made the claims in Grand Rapids on October 26 while campaigning for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers. Rogers is running against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who is Muslim and has an Arab family background.

“There are five hundred million Arabs in the world. And yet they don’t produce science,” Kennedy said, according to Michigan Advance. “They don’t win the Nobel Prize.”

The record includes winners from both science and literature. CAIR cited Egyptian-American chemist Ahmed Zewail, who won in 1999, and Egyptian novelist Naguib Mahfouz, who received the literature prize in 1988.

Omar Yaghi shared the 2025 chemistry prize with Richard Robson and Susumu Kitagawa. The UC Berkeley professor was born in Jordan to Palestinian refugees, according to his university.

Their work produced materials called metal-organic frameworks. Those structures have uses that include collecting water from dry air and trapping carbon dioxide. Yaghi’s award came the year before Kennedy’s claim.

Kennedy blamed the Muslim Brotherhood for the decline he alleged. El-Sayed has denied involvement with the group and publicly rejected it, Michigan Advance reported.

His public statements on science had drawn scrutiny before. AllHipHop previously covered Hillary Clinton’s criticism of Kennedy and President Donald Trump over their claims about vaccines and pregnancy medications in September 2025.

In Detroit, Kennedy instead discussed recovery services after visiting the Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network. Michigan Advance reported that he did not address the anti-Arab comments while taking questions.

The visit concerned STREETS, a federal program for people facing homelessness and serious mental illness or substance use disorders. HHS announced that Detroit’s Health Department was among eight recipients sharing $96 million. Each was set to receive $3 million annually for four years to connect treatment with housing and other recovery support.

item.title: Be’n Original Enters Crime Fiction With Debut Novel Power Kingdom
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Be'n Original swaps news deadlines for underworld fiction, introducing a debut thriller "Power Kingdom."
item.content:encoded:
Be’n Original, a former writer for AllHipHop, has evolved from covering culture to exploring criminal power in Power Kingdom, introducing his debut in fictional writing.

The veteran journalist and Urban Magazine publisher announced the urban crime thriller bringing his vast experience in entertainment media to a story about an expanding criminal empire.

For a writer whose bylines have appeared in AllHipHop, XXL, The Source, Vibe, King and Yahoo!, the move puts a different kind of storytelling at the center of his work. Instead of reporting on public figures and cultural developments, Be’n Original is introducing fictional characters whose personal relationships could threaten their survival.

Power Kingdom unfolds within a kingdom built on fear. According to the announcement, its premise draws inspiration from a popular colloquialism for Poughkeepsie, New York. The release does not identify that expression or provide further details about how the city informs the narrative.

The saga follows a growing criminal operation and a brotherhood operating in secrecy. The dangerous territory between them becomes a serious testing ground for loyalty as concealed motives emerge and relationships become liabilities.

The novel asks its characters to weigh love, honor, revenge and survival against one another. Closeness carries consequences in this world, where knowing someone’s secrets can create an advantage or expose a weakness. Friendship offers no guarantee of protection.

That focus gives the thriller a conflict beyond the expansion of a criminal enterprise. The announcement positions personal vulnerability as a central threat to authority, with those who command through intimidation facing the possibility that their control can collapse.

Be’n Original’s professional background includes journalism, publishing and creative direction.

The release is only the beginning and more on central characters are expected to be revealed.

The release date has not been announced yet.

Pre-orders for Power Kingdom by Be’n Original are now available: https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/X9RYANWSWVQSQ

item.title: Jennifer Lopez, Netflix & Robert Zemeckis Deny “The Last Mrs. Parrish” Clash
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jennifer Lopez, Robert Zemeckis and Netflix denied a report of a clash over the edit of their thriller "The Last Mrs. Parrish."
item.content:encoded:
Jennifer Lopez, Robert Zemeckis and Netflix jointly denied a report that the star and director were at odds over the edit of “The Last Mrs. Parrish.”

In a joint statement to Page Six, the three said: “Any suggestion that the filmmakers are not working in unison is without merit.”

The outlet cited unnamed sources who claimed Lopez had pushed to take control of the editing process after poor test screenings. It also reported that she and Zemeckis worked on a cut together last week and were expected to meet again next week.

Netflix disputed the account of the screenings, too, telling the outlet: “The film tested well, particularly with fans of Jennifer.”

Lopez has a producing role on the thriller as well as a starring part. Her Nuyorican Productions partners Elaine Goldsmith-Thomas and Benny Medina are also producers, alongside Molly Sims for Something Happy Productions and Liza Chasin for 3dot Productions.

That puts the singer and actress on both sides of the camera for a film whose shoot ended in November 2025, according to What’s on Netflix. Filming took place in New York and New Jersey.

The movie adapts “The Last Mrs. Parrish,” a novel by sisters Lynne Constantine and Valerie Constantine, who write together as Liv Constantine. Their website lists the Netflix adaptation as being in post-production.

Lopez plays Daphne Parrish opposite Nikolaj Coster-Waldau as her husband, Jackson. Isabel May plays Amber Patterson, the outsider who wants a place in their wealthy world. Amber builds a friendship with Daphne while pursuing Jackson, hoping to replace the wife.

Andrea Berloff, John Gatins and Lisa Rubin are the writers attached to the adaptation. The cast also includes Debi Mazar and Denis O’Hare.

Lopez brought experience as a producer and star to the project. She held both roles on “Hustlers”, the 2019 film directed by Lorene Scafaria. Its $33.2 million opening weekend was then the biggest for a live-action movie led by Lopez, passing the $23 million debut of “Monster-in-Law.”

“Hustlers” also brought Cardi B and Lizzo into an ensemble with Constance Wu, Julia Stiles and Keke Palmer. The film opened at No. 2 behind “It: Chapter Two.”

item.title: Lizzo Reveals How Dolly Parton Supported Her During Backlash
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Lizzo used her Dolly Parton Halloween tribute to recall a flute invitation, a special credit and support during public backlash.
item.content:encoded:
Lizzo said Dolly Parton asked her to play flute when she felt the world had turned its back. Her Halloween tribute came with a thank-you for that support.

“In 2024 when the world turned its back on me Dolly Parton asked me to play flute on her album,” Lizzo wrote in an Instagram photo gallery.

She said she agreed, with one request: credit for her flute persona, Sasha Flute. Parton did, Lizzo said. Their work also earned a plaque. She thanked Parton for seeing good in people during hard times.

The gallery followed a video of Lizzo in a yellow floral outfit and blonde wig inspired by Parton’s “Jolene” look. One photo placed Lizzo and a guitar in front of the framed album plaque.

Lizzo placed the invitation in 2024 in her caption. Parton’s Rockstar had already arrived on November 17, 2023, according to her official release announcement. Its track list named both Lizzo and Sasha Flute on “Stairway To Heaven.” Parton announced the album had earned RIAA gold status on March 14, 2024.

Former employees filed two separate lawsuits in 2023 with claims of sexual harassment, a hostile work environment and weight-shaming. Lizzo disputed the allegations and fought the claims in court.

In September, AllHipHop reported that a judge dismissed the claims left in wardrobe worker Asha Daniels’ case against Lizzo’s touring company. Lizzo had already been dismissed personally from that case. Daniels’ attorney challenged how the judge weighed the evidence. That lawsuit was separate from the case brought by three former dancers.

Lizzo had also spoken about the toll on her life with Willie Geist at Books of Wonder in New York. She was there to discuss her children’s book. She described trying to live with a public version of herself that she could no longer control.

She told Geist she wanted more focus on the work she was proud of. That included a book about a young girl finding her confidence, drawn from Lizzo’s own life and her flute character.

“I had to make peace with the fact that there’s a version of Lizzo that exists now that the world controls,” she told Geist.

item.title: Lil Real One’s Angola Killing Will Bring Murder Charge, Officials Say
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lil Real One's Angola killing is expected to bring a second-degree murder charge against another inmate, officials told WBRZ.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Real One‘s killing at Angola is expected to lead to a second-degree murder charge against another inmate, according to officials who spoke with WBRZ.

West Feliciana Parish Sheriff Brian Spillman told the station the 41-year-old rapper, whose real name was Brandon Guidry, died from injuries after a fight. Officials had not confirmed the other inmate’s identity when the report was published.

The planned charge follows the family’s earlier account of Lil Real One’s death, which AllHipHop covered before officials disclosed the expected murder charge.

Relatives previously told The Lens that Lil Real One was handcuffed and shackled when he was stabbed at the Louisiana State Penitentiary. That account came from his family. WBRZ’s report did not establish whether he was restrained during the attack.

His younger sister, Turiya Om Guidry, said she first learned what happened through calls from men inside Angola. When the family spoke with The Lens, relatives said prison officials had given them no information about the attack.

“Nobody from the prison called me and told me anything,” she told the outlet.

A Louisiana Department of Corrections spokesperson declined to discuss the incident on October 26, telling The Lens it was under investigation.

Lil Real One was serving life plus 50 years for a fatal French Quarter shooting. An Orleans Parish jury convicted him in December 2016 of second-degree murder and attempted second-degree murder, according to WVUE’s reporting carried by WAFB.

The March 21, 2015 shooting outside Last Call Bar and Grill, near Bourbon and Conti streets, killed 25-year-old musician Bruce Tims and wounded another man.

Court records cited by WVUE described a confrontation with the surviving victim before the shooting. Lil Real One sprayed that man with pepper spray, then returned about an hour later with a gun.

Before prison, Lil Real One grew up in New Orleans East and bonded with Soulja Slim.

The late rapper mentored him, gave him his rap name and signed him to Cut Throat Comitty Records, The Lens reported. His sister said Slim’s 2003 killing disrupted those music plans, though her brother kept recording in later years.

His sister also sought donations for funeral, cremation and other final expenses, according to WVUE.

item.title: SZA Heads To Tahiti To Work On New Album Amid Coachella Reports
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: SZA said she was headed to Tahiti to keep working on her next album as reports linked her to a Coachella 2027 headline slot.
item.content:encoded:
SZA said she was headed to Tahiti to keep working on her next album, sharing an album update as reports linked her to a Coachella headlining slot in 2027.

The singer posted the message on her alternate Instagram account alongside a screenshot of TMZ’s report about the festival’s prospective headliners. Her caption paired the music plans with doubts about taking on another big commitment.

“Headed to Tahiti to work this album some more. Mulling over big decisions. Saying yes when ur unprepared is crazy,” she wrote.

The message pointed to more work ahead on the record rather than a finished project. SZA did not name the album or give a release date in the caption. Her most recent studio album, SOS, arrived in 2022.

The festival discussion remained separate. SZA, Dua Lipa and Tame Impala were nearing agreements to headline, but Coachella organizers had not announced the official lineup. The report did not include an announcement from the festival.

A headlining appearance would build on several previous Coachella visits.

SZA performed there in 2018 and brought Kendrick Lamar onstage during her set. She returned as a surprise guest in April 2026, joining Justin Bieber to sing “Snooze.”

Between those festival appearances, she and Lamar shared the 2025 Super Bowl halftime stage and took their joint “Grand National Tour” on the road.

Her remarks about feeling unprepared also recalled concerns she had discussed before another major live undertaking.

In a June 2025 conversation with Chappell Roan for Interview magazine, SZA described anxiety before public appearances, including the “Grand National Tour” with Lamar.

“Every time I had to go on stage, every time I had to get on a carpet, I’d have full-on panic attacks,” she said.

During that earlier interview, she worried that audiences were coming for Lamar and questioned whether she had enough exciting new material to offer them. She also said she wanted to move ahead despite uncertainty, which helped explain the hesitation in her latest post.

Coachella 2027 is scheduled for April 9-11 and April 16-18 at the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California.

item.title: Bktherula Called Dad To Check Her Spanish, Then Put Him On “JEVITAS”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Bktherula explained how a call to her dad about her Spanish turned into a family collaboration while making "JEVITAS."
item.content:encoded:
Bktherula turned a Spanish check with her dad into a family feature on “JEVITAS,” explaining how a call home changed a song on her new album.

In an interview with Metal, she said the song took shape at an isolated mountain camp after a break in Ibiza. She called her father to check whether the Spanish she remembered made sense.

“But he told me it was fire, and I ended up getting him on the track,” she said.

Those recording trips can last two or three weeks, with producers joining her in places including Joshua Tree and the beach.

The song appeared on N5ON, released October 30 through Warner Records. The 14-track album also included “ACTIVATED” with Juicy J and “ADDICTED2U” featuring underscores, alongside the Whethan collaboration “I GO PUNK.”

The project began as an EP and grew into an album within roughly a year. She contacted underscores after one of her songs appeared in the producer’s set or remix and spread on Twitter.

Her interest in making room for different sounds was already clear when “I GO PUNK” arrived on May 29.

In a statement from Warner Records, Bktherula described setting aside genre expectations while making the song. She wanted something that captured the pleasure of being out with friends, with a loose approach to how it should sound.

Whethan brought his own history as a fan to the pairing. He said he had followed her work for years and had previously mentioned her on “Lock It Up,” his record with Yeat, midwxst and Matt Ox. He viewed their time in the studio as a chance to bring rap and electronic dance music together.

Bktherula told Metal her increasingly electronic sound developed naturally. She also named PinkPantheress among her current inspirations.

Their connection predated this album: PinkPantheress announced Bktherula as a supporting act on selected “Capable Of Love Tour” dates in November 2023. AllHipHop reported that announcement as PinkPantheress prepared a North American run, with Kanii also listed among the supporting acts.

As for her next move, Bktherula said she had already finished another album to follow N5ON.

item.title: Cardi B Urges Parents To Teach Kindness After Javits Frimpong Killing
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Cardi B linked bullying to gang pressure as she urged parents to raise kinder children after Javits Frimpong's killing.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B urged parents to confront bullying after the killing of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong. She tied the Bronx teenager’s death to her own experience of being picked on in New York.

“Teach your kids to be fucking kind because it starts with you,” Cardi said on Instagram Live. She said children needed those lessons as early as first grade.

The rapper described how being picked on could push a child toward a gang for protection. She connected that pressure to her own experience, explaining that she understood the search for a group “because that’s practically what happened to me.”

She criticized parents who dismissed teachers’ complaints about their children. Giving a child sneakers and attention did not excuse enabling cruel behavior, she said.

Cardi also described hostility toward newly arrived immigrant children. She said even American-born children whose families came from the same country could target them. She rejected the idea that one racial or ethnic group alone was responsible.

She rejected city public schools for her children.

Frimpong was fatally shot on his way to school in the Bronx on October 29. Police were seeking three teenage boys in connection with the shooting, ABC7 New York reported.

His father said he knew who was responsible. He told ABC7 that Frimpong had been bullied at school and that the students involved had recently been suspended.

The father had brought Frimpong from Ghana about a year earlier, hoping to give him a better life. Religious leaders, relatives and neighbors gathered Friday at the spot where the teen collapsed.

Leandra Feliz, whose son Junior Guzman was killed at 15 in 2018, also attended. “I’m only here to show support to the family,” she said.

The city Department of Education said it was providing counseling and supporting the NYPD investigation.

The family was also trying to bring his mother to New York to say goodbye. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Saturday that President Donald Trump had agreed to grant her a visa immediately. The White House had not confirmed that agreement when

The Associated Press reported. No arrests had been made at that point, and the killing remained under investigation.

item.title: Macklemore Defends Speaking On Gaza At London “Free Palestine Tour” Finale
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Macklemore closed his "Free Palestine Tour" in London with a speech about Gaza and a benefit lineup including Vic Mensa.
item.content:encoded:
Macklemore ended his “Free Palestine Tour” in London on Friday, October 30, telling fans that speaking about Gaza had become easier than keeping quiet. The sold-out benefit took place at OVO Arena Wembley.

“It was more uncomfortable for me to stay silent than to say something,” he said. He described speaking up as a human response, rather than an act of courage.

His remarks called for people to see children in Gaza as their own. He also questioned the barriers that divide people across borders.

Vic Mensa, Nemahsis, Paloma Faith and Shadia Mansour were among the artists on the London bill. Aja Monet, Cure for Paranoia and Lucas Jones also joined the lineup.

The venue’s event page pledged all concert proceeds to 12 organizations working with Palestinian communities. Recipients included Gaza Soup Kitchen, Medical Aid for Palestinians and the Palestine Children’s Relief Fund, along with Jewish Voice for Peace and UNRWA USA.

Organizers listed health care, education and direct humanitarian help, as well as community programs. The page also named advocacy, organizing and media efforts among the activities the concert would help fund.

The London finale followed a Dublin opening with Hozier and Kneecap. Dead Prez and Beoga also performed there.

The Dublin event also included a video appearance by the Gaza Children’s Choir, with Palestinian singer Lina Makoul starting the musical performances. Paris followed on Thursday, October 29, before London.

The series followed Macklemore losing his support slot on Ed Sheeran’s U.S. tour after his September speeches at MetLife Stadium.

Sheeran attributed the decision to tour organizers and later apologized for how he handled the dispute.

Patriots owner Robert Kraft said Macklemore’s rhetoric and imagery offended Jewish people and opposed his planned appearance at Gillette Stadium. The rapper rejected that view. He said criticizing Israel did not mean opposing Jewish people and called for everyone to be treated equally.

In London, Macklemore also addressed the 50 members of the House of Lords who had sought to stop his concert. He responded by stressing equal rights for people everywhere.

item.title: Adamn Killa Sends Loyola Crowd To Whole Foods After Campus Blockade
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Adamn Killa moved his Loyola meetup to Whole Foods after a campus road closure sent students chasing his Cybertruck.
item.content:encoded:
Adamn Killa’s return to Loyola University Chicago ended up in a Whole Foods parking lot after a road barricade blocked his arrival earlier this week.

Hundreds of students had gathered near the Information Commons for the rapper’s planned 4 p.m. appearance, The Loyola Phoenix reported. Campus Safety and Chicago police had closed Loyola Campus Road to keep fans from surrounding his vehicle.

Some had waited more than an hour to see him. By the time he reached campus, he was over 45 minutes late.

Unable to enter, he left and posted a new destination on Instagram. “Come to the Whole Foods down the street now,” he wrote.

Students ran through the neighborhood to meet him. Wearing pink and green, Adamn stood in his Cybertruck’s bed and invited the crowd to make a TikTok. The gathering ended when sirens approached, and he said police had arrived.

The detour followed a packed Loyola appearance a year earlier.

On October 16, 2025, students crowded around his SUV so tightly he struggled to open its door, according to the campus paper’s account. Some climbed trees or stood on trash cans for a better view.

That visit grew out of a TikTok choice between Loyola and Columbia College. Students urged him to pick Loyola, then gathered for selfies and a group video.

“If you’re Sister Jean, this is for you,” Adamn said before dancing with the crowd.

His signature “This is for you” videos paired a dedication to a specific audience with his 2025 song “Fall On.” Campus Safety eventually asked him to leave. Fans chased his vehicle as he departed.
